kev_floor.justification: KEV listing means exploitation has been confirmed in the wild, so a reachable KEV CVE should never rank as unlikely, even when its EPSS is low (common for ICS CVEs). 0.5 treats it as at least a coin flip once the attacker can reach it.
kev_floor.source: CISA KEV catalog (BOD 22-01) confirms active exploitation in the wild; 0.5 is a deliberate design choice.

default_credentials.justification: Default passwords are public and tried automatically by scanners and botnets; failure mostly comes from the device being changed or unreachable, not from difficulty.
default_credentials.source: CISA/FBI Joint Advisory AA23-335A (IRGC exploitation of Unitronics default credentials in water sector).

exposed_remote_access_no_mfa.justification: Needs a working credential (guessing, stuffing or a leaked password), so harder than defaults but realistic over time for an internet-facing service.

anomaly_boost_alpha.justification: An anomaly is a signal, not proof of compromise. A score of 1.0 closes 30% of the remaining gap to certainty (p' = p + (1 - p) * 0.3 * score), so the ML raises priority without overriding the vulnerability evidence.

mfa_reduction_factor.justification: Multiplies credential-attack probability by 0.1 (90% reduction). Deliberately more conservative than vendor 99.9% claims to account for targeted bypasses (push fatigue, adversary-in-the-middle, session token theft).
mfa_reduction_factor.source: Microsoft Security Blog (Aug 2019) reported 99.9% protection; we use 90% as a conservative design choice.

consequence_weights.justification: Physical safety dominates in critical infrastructure; people affected comes next; duration matters but is partly captured by the other two. Sum = 1.0.
consequence_weights.source: Consequence-first framing follows INL Consequence-driven Cyber-informed Engineering (CCE).

consequence_normalisation.justification: Normalises severity (0-4 / 4), people affected (/ 500,000 city population), and outage duration (/ 72 h max scenario duration).

opportunistic.name: Opportunistic Cybercriminal
opportunistic.justification: Mass-scanning attackers go for exposed, known-exploited weaknesses and do not chain long paths into OT.

nation_state.name: State-Sponsored APT
nation_state.justification: Patient, well-resourced actors chain through IT and DMZ into control layers and use third-party access.

insider.name: Disgruntled / Compromised Insider
insider.justification: Models an employee or stolen employee account with valid domain credentials: no need to break in, only to move laterally.

patch_it.justification: Standard OS/app patch plus a reboot, usually possible within the month.

patch_ot.justification: Firmware updates on controllers need vendor validation, testing and a process shutdown, so they are deferred to scheduled windows.

segment_rule.justification: Rule change plus testing that operations traffic still flows; no process stop needed.

disable_remote_access.justification: Quick to switch off; operational vendor support SLA must be handled procedurally.

add_mfa.justification: Enrolment and testing for remote-access gateway users.

enhanced_monitoring.justification: Detection, not prevention: raises confidence, does not lower likelihood.
